$comment: Rate limits for services/control-api, per plan 02 CP-5.
A file rather than constants in code: an operator responding to an incident
changes a limit by editing this and restarting, not by opening a pull request.
Loaded and validated by src/config/rate-limits.ts; an invalid file refuses to boot.
perMinute — sustained rate: how fast the bucket refills.
burst     — bucket capacity: how many requests may arrive at once.
scope     — 'organization' keys the bucket by organization (falling back to the
user, then the client address, when a request names none); 'ip' keys
it by client address alone, which is what an unauthenticated brute
force has to be counted by.
whenUnavailable — what to do when Redis cannot answer. 'allow' keeps the API up
at the cost of a missed window; 'deny' keeps the protection at the
cost of the route. Reads and mutations fail open because a limiter
that takes the control plane down is worse than one that misses a
window. Auth fails closed because password-adjacent brute-force
protection that evaporates the moment a cache blips is not
protection at all.
proxy     — how far to believe X-Forwarded-For. An ip-scoped limit only limits
a client if the address it counts is the client's, and this service
runs in a container behind a proxy. Set trustedHops to the number of
proxies in front of it (1 for a single load balancer), OR list their
addresses in trustedProxies — never both. Both default to trusting
nothing, which counts socket addresses: wrong behind a proxy, but
never attacker-chosen. Trusting the header unconditionally would let
any caller pick their own bucket and bypass every ip-scoped limit.

proxy.note: Set trustedHops to 1 once this service is deployed behind the edge proxy.

auth.note: The credential surface: /v1/auth/* except the device poll. Per client address.

device.note: POST /v1/auth/device/token only — a machine polling at the interval GET /v1/auth/device told it to. Must stay above 60 / DEVICE_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS a minute and above the polls one grant window produces; test/plugins.test.ts pins both against the source constants. Guessing is not the threat here (a device code is 32 bytes of CSPRNG), so this is sized for the poll rather than against a search.

mutations.note: Every other method outside /v1/auth — POST, PATCH, PUT, DELETE.
